title: Lens power & combinations
examples: How do I find the total power of two lenses together?
What does the unit dioptre mean for lens power?
If I put two lenses together, do I just add their powers?

explain.say: Today we look at lens power measured in dioptres.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a convex lens. Look at the convex lens, the object and the focal point. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The power in dioptres is the reciprocal of the focal length in metres.
A converging lens has a positive focal length and positive power.
When combining lenses, you add their individual powers together.
For example, a lens of 2 dioptres and one of 3 dioptres combine to 5 dioptres.
In real life, reading glasses combine the power needed for near and far vision.

faq.q: What is the difference between focal length and power?
faq.a: Focal length is the distance in metres where parallel rays meet. Power is the measure of the lens's ability to bend light, measured in dioptres.
asks: Is power just a number for the lens?

faq.q: If I use two lenses, do I always add the powers?
faq.a: Yes, for thin lenses placed in contact, you find the total power by adding the individual powers together.
asks: Can I subtract the powers sometimes?
Does the order matter when adding powers?

faq.q: What does a negative power mean for a lens?
faq.a: A negative power means the lens is diverging, which spreads out light rays instead of bringing them together.
asks: What kind of lens has negative power?
Does negative power mean it's broken?

faq.q: Do I have to convert anything before I calculate the power?
faq.a: Yes, you must always make sure that any focal length given is in metres before calculating the power in dioptres.
asks: What units must the focal length be in?
Can I use centimetres for focal length?

faq.q: What if the lenses are separated by a distance?
faq.a: The simple addition rule only works for lenses placed in direct contact. Separation changes the calculation significantly.
asks: Is there a formula for separated lenses?

facts: Lens power is measured in the unit dioptre, symbol D.
Power is the reciprocal of the focal length measured in metres.
A converging lens has positive power, and a diverging lens has negative power.
The total power of multiple thin lenses in contact is the sum of their individual powers.

quiz.say: A lens has a focal length of 0 point 5 metres. What is its power?
quiz.why: The power is the reciprocal of the focal length in metres, so one divided by point five is two.

wrong.1: This is wrong because the power is the reciprocal, not the value itself.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you must use the focal length in metres for the calculation.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the focal length must be in metres, not centimetres.

quiz.say: If you combine a 3 dioptre lens and a 4 dioptre lens, what is the total power?
quiz.why: When thin lenses are in contact, you simply add their individual powers together.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the result must be in dioptres, not metres.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you should add the powers, not multiply them.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you must add the powers together to find the total.

quiz.say: A lens has a focal length of negative 1 metre. What is its power?
quiz.why: The power is the reciprocal of the focal length, and the negative sign indicates it is a diverging lens.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you must keep the negative sign from the focal length.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the power is defined by the reciprocal of the focal length.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the answer must have the unit of dioptres.
